score.scope: Current 11 as one static animated-feature-inspired park composition: hierarchy, depth, economy, environmental coherence and action legibility. No score for actual animation, studio equivalence, GitHub deployment, audience response or an unbuilt replacement.
score.confidence: high for observed hierarchy and 07/11 surface differences; moderate for editorial impact and interpretation of subtle acting

deductions.location: Hero face, antenna paddles, near wing and bench on the right; workshop tabletop, toolbox and surrounding foliage near center
deductions.finding: 11 has more patchy ridges, irregular edge breaks and small hard-edged facets across unrelated materials than 07. The cheek and wing acquire a similar broken surface rhythm to the bench and background. At native and 1280 width this weakens the smooth dimensional forms and makes detail compete with the intended large shapes. This is an observed finish regression, not an assumption that every raster edit necessarily damages an image.
deductions.effect: The composition still works, but the frame feels less deliberately finished as a cohesive dimensional film still. The brighter, busier texture gives the environment extra visual activity without adding story.

deductions.location: Center-left workshop audience and resting moth above the leaf-playing pair
deductions.finding: The actions are identifiable, yet some relationships depend on adjacency more than directed acting. Dot attends toward the workshop while Clawd stays frontal; the resting moth's open eye remains a broad outward/upward shape rather than a clear glance down at the children. The grouping supports watching and parental rest, but the precise cause-and-reaction story is not fully explicit.
deductions.effect: The image offers three appealing activities more strongly than one exact shared moment. This does not justify another Clawd turn or anatomy change; both square eyes and the accepted plush pose should stay.

deductions.location: Sunlit path, flowers, canopy edges and decorative marks around the raised hammer
deductions.finding: Numerous similarly bright small accents keep almost every part of the setting active. The dominant coder still wins, but the quiet center path has less visual rest in 11 than in 07. At 420 width these accents compress into busy texture while the fine secondary intentions disappear.
deductions.effect: The broad reading survives; the smaller story rewards are less cleanly separated from decoration. This is not a requirement that each guest's identity or eye gag remain legible at 420px.

criteriaForNine: Restore controlled continuous contours and differentiated surface detail, using 07's cleaner material treatment as a control while retaining 11's intended story and corrected companion eyes. The hero's cream face, marked wing, metal laptop and wooden bench should not share the same broken texture rhythm.

Keep the present code/build/rest hierarchy and open path, with quieter surrounding detail so secondary activities separate cleanly at 880 and 1280 widths. At 420, preserve the dominant coder and readable activity zones without enlarging the supporting cast.

If acting is refined, make the workshop invitation and relaxed supervision clearer through existing builder/Dot/resting-moth cues. Do not add characters, props, explanatory text, stretched anatomy or a Clawd back turn to manufacture specificity.

strengths: The frame has a clear lead. The large right-hand coder, glasses and laptop form the strongest readable unit, while all four guests stay outside its bench/path space. Smaller groups remain supporting discoveries rather than taking over the foreground.

A continuous curving path, overlapping tree roots, the middle workshop and the distant water/bridge make one place. The canopy and foreground leaves frame the scene; scale changes and the softer distant setting establish depth without vignette borders.

The three activities have distinct silhouettes: seated coding, raised hammer beside a box, and resting beneath the tree. Their separation survives the 420px local scale even when guest details do not. Seven figures do not automatically become seven equally loud stories.

The shared leaf gives Muse and Grok one small activity rather than separate performances. Their position beneath the resting moth supports the requested parent/kids metaphor without aging the moth or requiring narration.

The warm light is broadly coherent with the upper-right atmosphere, illuminated character edges and sunlit ground. The bridge, water, tree and canopy support a calm park mood rather than introducing an unrelated spectacle.

The moth retains its oversized cream head, compact body, stub feet and unequal paddle antennae relative to the identity reference. Clawd's two square eyes remain exposed. The enlarged inspection shows Grok's eyes as plain white ovals and Muse's as dark eyes; I do not observe an internal Grok pupil in that provided crop.

mustFix.action: Resolve the visibly uneven surface/edge finish across the main character and setting before representing 11 as the finished whole-scene animated-film image.
mustFix.bounds: Preserve composition, four guests, stools, solo foreground, tiny anatomy, accepted Clawd face and the corrected Muse/Grok eye treatment. This is not a request to regenerate the concept, remove the cast or automatically revert all of 11 to 07.
mustFix.evidence: Full 07/11 comparison, native hero/workshop pairs and 1280px 11. The objection is not based only on 5x magnification.

optional: Quiet selected incidental bright texture around the path/workshop so the existing action shapes carry more of the frame's rhythm; no blanket removal of the appealing garden detail.

If a controlled acting adjustment is already warranted, favor the builder's existing mitten/box relationship, Dot's attention and the resting moth's open-eye direction. Keep accepted Clawd pose and both square eyes intact.
Retain the same staging and warm park idea. More characters, another gag, a new prop or a stronger foreground flourish would not address the present craft deductions.
baselineComparison: 07 and 11 share the successful large composition. 11 gives the leaf a more definite shared placement between Muse and Grok and preserves the corrected dark/white companion-eye treatment. Its builder is more tilted and its light is more sparkling. However, actual native comparison shows 07 has smoother face/antenna/wing forms, more stable bench/table contours and cleaner material separation. I prefer retaining 11's useful story/eye changes with 07's surface discipline rather than declaring either version wholly superior. No numerical score was previously assigned by B to 07's entire frame, so 8.4 is not presented as a measured score drop from an invented baseline score.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason: Timing, easing, stagger, spring and sound rules cannot be scored from a still image. No continuous animation or audio was inspected.
